items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: I imagine you know of my uncle in Chicago... His name is Natty Dominique

ctx.x: What's your name? Well, sure, Paul. I'll be happy to. My name is Don Albert, professionally, and my family name is Dominique. I imagine you know of my uncle in Chicago. He still uses his name Dominique. His name is Natty Dominique, one of the first trumpet players to leave from New Orleans along with King Oliver and the other guys. And after this, where you are now, we're in San Antonio, Texas. This is my residence, and it's 715 St. James. Been living here for the last five years in this home. We bought this…
This is June the 6th, 1961, and I'm Paul Crawford. You were talking about this fellow, one of the first guys you took, you know, when you left New Orleans? No. A banjo player or something?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Uncle Natty and I were, he was one of my favorite uncles... I visited him quite a number of times.

ctx.x: You learn something new every day.

You see, I studied the music, which was something in my favor. As I always said, the background of the family is very musical. My grandmother and grandfather were singers. Had a knot that played the piano. One uncle that played the violin. One played the cornet. Two of them because Natty is still living. And he doesn't play anymore. He still has his horn. But even on, we can go back and just name just schools or something that wasn't in the family that were musically inclined. And I hope that that's where I got…
What about Natty? Did you know Natty Dominique when he was down here?
